- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.30) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.30), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., 70+), leading to exaggerated highs in next period; cap or smooth upward momentum.
- Mean reversion bias: if price has been rising sharply for 3+ days, model often fails to anticipate pullback; reduce forecast slope slightly.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in capturing sentiment shifts — especially when sentiment turns sharply; align forecast with sentiment change lag (e.g., 2–3 days).
- If sentiment history shows repeated volatility (e.g., alternating +/–0.30), model tends to overfit short-term noise; dampen forecast variance.
